title: Streaming Parse Guardian & Repair Playground: token-level repairs and graceful fallback for constrained decoding
creator: Liam Chen
description: Prototype a Streaming Parse Guardian (SPG) - a token-granular monitoring and repair layer that runs alongside streaming responses to enforce JSON/schema contracts while supporting function/toolcall interleavings. The goal is to reduce customer-facing schema failures by applying lightweight, deterministic repairs or safe fallbacks before surfacing errors to callers. This ticket covers design, harness, and an initial canary implementation that integrates with the runtime's streaming pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: SPG component can detect schema contract violations on partial streams and produce a canonical repair suggestion within 50ms on median
Repair-first policy reduces observed schema-failure rate on our canary traffic by >= 60% compared to baseline (no repair)
System exposes telemetry: violation_count, repair_attempts, repair_success_rate, fallback_rate, and avg_repair_latency
Playground includes failure injection controls for: truncated JSON, interleaved tool-call tokens, token-loss, and deliberate hallucinated fields
Canary rollout (1% traffic) with automatic rollback if customer_impact becomes medium or higher
steps: Design: define parse-state machine and repair strategies (closing braces, injecting missing keys with null, reordering arrays for partial emits)
Impl: lightweight streaming hook inside runtime that maintains incremental parse checkpoints (byte/token offsets + simple AST stubs)
Repair policies: repair-first, try-toolcall-reconcile, and conservative-fallback-only
Testing harness: extend existing chaos-fuzz harness to simulate interleaved tool calls and truncated token streams
Canary: mirror 1% of production traffic through SPG in read-only mode, then enable repair-first on 0.5% if metrics look good
Docs: docblock for SDK behavior when repair or fallback occurs and operator runbook for debugging
experiment_results: Initial lab fuzzing against Mistral-Chat-instruct family: baseline schema-violation-rate=4.2% over 10k prompts; with repair-first reduced to 1.5% (repair_success_rate=68%)
Simulated token-loss (drop 1/200 tokens): repair_success_rate drops to 54% for long-nested objects, fallback_rate increases to 8%
Function-call interleaving test: 3% of failures caused by tool-call boundary tokens; new token-aware sentinel logic resolved 80% of those cases
Repair median latency: 42ms on c6g-medium-like test harness; 95th percentile 210ms (optimizations planned to reduce p95)
Cost: prototype adds ~1.8% CPU overhead in streaming path on our dedicated pool baseline
comments: 2026-02-15 Liam Chen: Created ticket. Goal is to implement a non-invasive hook that can attempt deterministic repairs on partial JSON streams before failing downstream callers. Initial idea: incremental parse checkpoints + small set of repair heuristics prioritized from lowest-risk to highest-visibility changes.

2026-02-18 Aisha Kapoor: Design review notes - prefer token-indexed checkpointing instead of byte offsets to support multi-encoding clients. Add acceptance criterion for repair latency. Suggest adding a 'repaired_payload' flag to telemetry so downstream consumers can opt-in to stricter verification.

2026-02-22 Marco Rivera: Engineering sync - agreed on three repair strategies: syntactic-close (append closing tokens), best-effort-infer (add missing keys with null), toolcall-reconcile (pause repair until tool-call boundary confirmed). Need to ensure repairs are fully replayable for audits.

2026-02-25 Priya Singh: QA note - will extend chaos harness to inject 'late_toolcall' sequences. Also propose a prioritized test matrix (short vs long sequences, nested depth 1/3/6, token-drop rate 0/0.5/1%)

2026-03-01 Aisha Kapoor: Implemented prototype hook and wired up basic telemetry. Running 50k-canary-sim locally. Found a regression where repair-first caused incorrect reconstitution for arrays-of-objects when elements emit in two separate partial emits; introduced array-reassembly rule that buffers up to 256 tokens for array elements (configurable).

2026-03-03 Liam Chen: Can confirm integration test with tool-calling harness passed for Mistral and Llama families. Pushing PR for initial review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2245. Next: add graded rollout and operator runbook.
